messages.author: 05954d53fb9c89d2
messages.subject: multivariate normal distribution
parts:
Hi all,
I have a general/basic question about the prior distribution.
If my dependent variable y is a linear function of 2 independent variables x1 and x2. When should I choose multivariate normal distributions over univariate normal distributions for coefficients on x1 and x2? That is, when should I believe the coefficients on x1 and x2 are correlated and model that structure?
What problems will I have if I modeled the correlated coefficients on x1 and x2 as 2 univariate normally distributed parameters?

Thank you very much
Best
Jing

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] multivariate normal distribution
parts:
You say x1 and x2 are independent...

If x1 and x2 are independent in the statistical sense, your
posteriors on the predictors should remain independent.

If x1 and x2 are independent in the sense of being arguments,
then you might want to inspect the posterior for their coefficients
when you have independent priors.

But, if you only have one coefficient for each predictor (no
hierarchical structure), then the only thing you can do is give
them some fixed correlation in the prior---you can't fit the
dependency.

- Bob

Hi Bob,
Thank you for your response.
By "independent variables x1 and x2", I basically meant x1 and x2 are 2 covariates. I didn't mean anything about their statistical dependency.
How can I know whether the posterior for their coefficients (i.e., beta1 and beta2) are correlated when I have independent priors?
Also, what do you mean by "give them some fixed correlation in the prior"? Do you mean, for example, x1 is the weight of a car, x2 is the length of a car, and y is the price of a car. Now, I consider a third variable x3-- the maker of a car, and assume beta1 and beta2 are different for different makers? 

Thank you very much for your help
Best
Jing

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] multivariate normal distribution
parts:
Create a scatterplot of the posteriors. In RStan, there's
a pairs() function which you can configure with the parameters
you want to look at. Or view them in ShinyStan.

Because you don't have replications of the coefficients, it's
hard to get any mileage about having correlation on their prior
unless you know what it is. You can have the coefficients for
x1 and x2 vary by maker if you want to build a hierarchical model.
That's where you'd use an unknown correlation prior.

There's nothing intrinsically problematic about correlation in
the posterior---we get it all the time in GLMs.

- Bob
